title: Metropolitan Manila Development Authority v. Concerned Residents of Manila Bay
summary: The Supreme Court issued a continuing mandamus ordering government agencies to clean up and rehabilitate Manila Bay. The Court held that the government has a ministerial duty to enforce environmental laws and that citizens have the right to compel such enforcement.
doctrine: Government agencies tasked with environmental protection have a ministerial duty to enforce environmental laws. The right to a balanced and healthful ecology may be enforced through a writ of continuing mandamus. The Court may compel government agencies to perform their duties under environmental statutes.
fullText:
VELASCO, JR., J.:

The case involves a petition for mandamus to compel government agencies to clean up, rehabilitate, and preserve Manila Bay.

The Constitution guarantees the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology. Various environmental laws impose duties on government agencies to protect and preserve the country's water resources, including Manila Bay.

The Court issues a continuing mandamus directing the concerned government agencies to undertake the cleanup, rehabilitation, and preservation of Manila Bay. The continuing mandamus is warranted because the duty to protect the environment is a ministerial function that the government agencies are mandated by law to perform.
